We need an integer \(n<2010\) such that

\[
n\equiv 5 \pmod 7,\qquad n\equiv 10 \pmod{11},\qquad n\equiv 10 \pmod{13}.
\]

Since \(n\equiv 10\pmod{11}\) and \(n\equiv 10\pmod{13}\), we have

\[
n\equiv 10 \pmod{143}.
\]

So write

\[
n=143k+10.
\]

Now impose the condition modulo \(7\):

\[
143k+10\equiv 5 \pmod 7.
\]

Since \(143\equiv 3\pmod 7\) and \(10\equiv 3\pmod 7\),

\[
3k+3\equiv 5 \pmod 7
\]

\[
3k\equiv 2 \pmod 7.
\]

The inverse of \(3\) modulo \(7\) is \(5\), so

\[
k\equiv 10\equiv 3 \pmod 7.
\]

Thus

\[
k=7m+3.
\]

Then

\[
n=143(7m+3)+10=1001m+439.
\]

We need the largest such \(n<2010\):

\[
1001m+439<2010
\]

\[
1001m<1571
\]

\[
m\le 1.
\]

So the largest value is when \(m=1\):

\[
n=1001+439=1440.
\]

\[
\boxed{1440}
\]
